metadata.note: The East Tennessee, Virginia and Georgia, 1869-1894: formed Nov 26 1869 by consolidating the East Tennessee and Virginia (Bristol - Knoxville) and the East Tennessee and Georgia (Knoxville - Dalton, Cleveland - Chattanooga), it grew by purchase in 1880-82 into a system from Bristol to Chattanooga, Atlanta, Macon and the sea at Brunswick, and from Rome through Selma to Meridian, with branches to the North Carolina line and Hawkinsville. Sold in foreclosure 1886 and reorganised as the ETV&G Railway; controlled by the Richmond Terminal 1887-1892; receivers from 1892; sold to the Southern Railway Jul 7 1894. Fourteen features, every one drawn only for its confirmed ETV&G years (the report's drawable spans): the main line Bristol - Chattanooga (geometry shared with the Southern feature in knoxville_early_railroads.geojson, which now starts 1894), Cleveland - Dalton, the 1883 Ooltewah cut-off, Dalton - Rome, Rome - Atlanta, Atlanta - Macon, Macon - Brunswick, the Hawkinsville branch, Rome - Selma, Selma - Meridian, Morristown - Wolf Creek in two operators (Cincinnati, Cumberland Gap and Charleston 1871-1872, ETV&G 1872-1894), Wolf Creek - Paint Rock, and the Clinton - Harriman Junction (Walden's Ridge) line as a single-year anchor. The ETV&G's 1877-1887 operation of the Memphis and Charleston is drawn as two ETV&G features inside florence_muscle_shoals_railroads.geojson, on that file's M&C geometry.
metadata.ownership_split: Predecessors -> ETV&G: ET&V and ET&G Nov 26 1869 (split 1869; the predecessor features are in knoxville_early_railroads.geojson); CCG&C -> ETV&G Nov 14 1872 (split 1872, both features here); Georgia Southern (Dalton - Rome) Nov 6 1880 (drawn from 1881); SR&D Alabama receivers Feb 11 1881; Alabama Central Jun 15 1881; Macon and Brunswick Jun 14 1881; Walden's Ridge Apr 20 1888. Memphis and Charleston leased Jul 1 1877 - Apr 29 1887 (split in florence_muscle_shoals_railroads.geojson). ETV&G -> Southern Jul 7 1894 (every feature ends 1894). NOT splits: the 1886 Railroad -> Railway reorganisation; Richmond Terminal control 1887-1892; the 1892-1894 receivership; the Cincinnati and Georgia's paper title 1881-82; the Richmond and Danville's annulled lease Jul 1 - Dec 7 1888 (inside one year).
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: [6] Rogersville branch (ETV&G 1889-1894 has no passenger source; 1873-1889 horse-worked or other operators); [7] Knoxville and Augusta (run independently under its own name -- a separate company, own queue item); [8] Knoxville and Ohio (separate queue item, ETV&G-operated 1881-1894 per Harrison); [10] Embreeville branch (ore, no passenger evidence); [18] Rome and Decatur, Rome - Attalla (no ETV&G passenger timetable); [19] Cincinnati, Selma and Mobile, Marion Junction - Akron (no ETV&G-era passenger evidence; a Sep 1894 Southern time card is a hint only); [20] Brierfield, Blocton and Birmingham (coal, not attributable); [21] Mobile and Birmingham (operator unsettled; 1892 through cars prove service, not who ran it); [22] the rest of the Memphis and Charleston (Memphis - Corinth, Decatur - Stevenson -- not drawn for any era); [23] Somerville branch; [24]-[27] controlled but separately operated roads (AGS/CNO&TP, Louisville Southern, Gadsden and Attalla, Belt Ry of Chattanooga, WNC). Also not drawn: the predecessors' years on Cleveland - Dalton (ET&G 1852-1869) and the pre-ETV&G operators of Dalton - Rome - Selma, Selma - York and Macon - Brunswick, which belong to their own queue items; the ~5 WNC miles Paint Rock - Warm Springs; the Big Mountain coal spur.
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. Coal and ore branches with no passenger evidence (Coal Creek - Cambria, Briceville - Panola, Oliver Springs - Big Mountain, Embreeville, the BB&B, the Belt Railway of Chattanooga) are not drawn. Every feature ends with the ETV&G in 1894.
metadata.horsecar_check: None drawn. The only animal traction found on the system -- the Rogersville branch north of the Holston, horse-worked from Dec 1873 -- is not drawn.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: 1. [OPEN] start: ccgc-morristown-wolf-creek begins 1871 because the first timetable seen is Sep 1871; the line opened 1869 (Harrison) and 1869-1870 are withheld, not denied. Who ran its trains Sep 1871 - Nov 1872 (CCG&C by the timetable heading, or the ET&V/ETV&G on whose tariff it worked) is also open. 2. [ANCHOR]: etvg-clinton-harriman is drawn for 1890 only, the one confirmed passenger year; 1888-1889 and 1891-1894 are likely but unsourced. The branchline.uk Fowler station lists (tennesseerrs.pdf, georgiarrs.pdf, alabamarrs.pdf) could not be fetched on 2026-10-28 and would settle this and the omitted branches. 3. The Ooltewah cut-off's passenger use is inferred from its purpose; no timetable names it. 4. Selma - Meridian: the York - Lauderdale grade is an identification of an untagged-name OSM abandoned way, and 5.1 mi of it are a straight line; when the ETV&G-era Lauderdale routing gave way to the AGS trackage from York is not dated. 5. Macon - Brunswick mileage, 174 (railga.com) vs ~190 (trace 188.6). 6. All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates (see each segment note and speed_source).
conflicts: Bristol - Knoxville opening day: Oct 8 1858 (Harrison p.663) vs May 14 1858 (Wikipedia) -- before this layer's span.
Macon - Brunswick completion 1870 vs 1871 (Harrison's table vs text) -- before this layer's span.
Selma - Meridian: Harrison p.677 and the 1882 circular route via Lauderdale and the Mobile and Ohio; Harrison's 1901 table via AGS trackage from York. The former is drawn.

Memphis and Charleston lease: the ETV&G's 1878 report calls it an 'alliance' leaving M&C officers 'substantially in control'; the 1882 circular runs it as an ETV&G division. The split follows the circular.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs: the same 681-point line as the Southern Railway Bristol - Chattanooga feature in knoxville_early_railroads.geojson, copied verbatim for the Rule 4 split. Traced 245.0 mi against 241.55 mi documented (Harrison 1901, ETV&G line of road Bristol - Chattanooga): Bristol - Knoxville 131.6 mi (~130 documented), Knoxville - Cleveland 82.6 mi, Cleveland - Chattanooga 30.8 mi (29.12 documented). LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the modern Norfolk Southern line; the 1940s TVA reservoir relocations along the Tennessee River (Fort Loudoun, Watts Bar) and later terminal rearrangements at Knoxville and Chattanooga are not backed out, so in those places the 1869-1894 trains are drawn on later track. The line was 5 ft gauge until the 1886 southern gauge change. Ends 212 m short of Bristol Union Station and 368 m short of the Chattanooga Terminal Station site, where OSM track ends; the ETV&G's own Chattanooga terminal (Union Depot) is not separately located.

segments.note: The East Tennessee, Virginia and Georgia main line: the East Tennessee and Virginia (Bristol - Knoxville) and East Tennessee and Georgia (Knoxville - Cleveland - Chattanooga) consolidated Nov 26 1869 (Harrison pp.664-684). Part of the Virginia, Tennessee and Georgia Air Line through route New York - Washington - Lynchburg - Bristol - Chattanooga/Atlanta. Dated passenger touch-downs: the Morristown Gazette printed the ETV&G main-line Mail and Express times at Morristown weekly 1871-1881; the July 1882 circular puts Bristol - Chattanooga in the East Tennessee division (HQ Knoxville); the 1883 Air Line guidebook describes it; the Mar 20 1892 time card shows Cleveland - Knoxville - Morristown - Bristol trains with New York Pullmans via the Shenandoah Valley. Knoxville - Chattanooga trains kept to Cleveland after the 1883 Ooltewah cut-off, which served Chattanooga - Atlanta traffic. Moved here from the Southern Railway feature in knoxville_early_railroads.geojson (Rule 4). Ends 1894: sold to the Southern Railway at Knoxville Jul 7 1894 (possession of most lines Aug 1 1894); the Southern-era continuation is not drawn in this layer. The Richmond and Danville's lease of the whole system (effective Jul 1 1888, surrendered Dec 7 1888 after the Knoxville Chancery Court annulled it) is a five-month interlude inside one calendar year and is not split out; nor are the 1886 reorganisation (Railroad -> Railway Company), Richmond Terminal stock control 1887-1892 or the 1892-1894 receivership, all of which left the same company running the trains. Frequency estimated from the 1892 time card's train count, not a sourced headway.

segments.note: Opened Morristown - Wolf Creek 'about forty miles, in the year 1869' by the Cincinnati, Cumberland Gap and Charleston, worked under the East Tennessee and Virginia's tariff (Harrison p.~793). THE 1871 START IS THE FIRST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT THE OPENING [OPEN start]: the first printed timetable seen is the Morristown Gazette of Sep 13 1871 -- 'Cincinnati, Cumberland Gap & Charleston R.R. Daily trains (Sunday excepted) leave Morristown at 10:45 a.m. arrive at Wolf Creek at 2:00 p.m.' (also Oct and Dec 1871, Feb and Aug 1872). 1869-1870 are withheld, not denied; do not extend without a timetable. Who ran the trains Sep 1871 - Nov 1872 is itself open: the timetable heading says the CCG&C; Harrison has it on the ET&V/ETV&G tariff. Ends Nov 14 1872, when McGhee and Wilson took title at the State-lien sale in trust for the ETV&G, which went into possession and operated it (Harrison p.709). Wolf Creek was the railhead for Warm Springs, NC, eight miles on by coach. Frequency: one daily train each way (timetable), headway taken as a day.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] ONE PROVEN PASSENGER YEAR, NOT THE SPAN OF SERVICE. Through line Clinton - Harriman Junction opened by the ETV&G in June 1888 (Harrison p.~907; ETV&G from Apr 20 1888), over and beyond the narrow-gauge Walden's Ridge Railroad's Oakdale Furnace - Oliver Springs iron and coal road of 1883. The only passenger year confirmed is 1890: The Maryville Times (9 Apr, 30 Apr, 21 May, 28 May 1890, p.5) lists Knoxville train times including 'Walden's Ridge Railroad. For Cincinnati 8:30 pm ... From 7:55 a m' -- a Knoxville - Clinton - Harriman Junction - Cincinnati passenger route advertised under the old name. The ETV&G ran it: in Aug 1892 its receivers offered rewards against miners who seized 'the engines and cars of the East Tennessee, Virginia and Georgia railway on its Walden's Ridge division ... thereby preventing the running of trains' (Savannah Tribune 27 Aug 1892 p.1). Service certainly ran wider than 1890 both ways (1888-1889 and 1891-1894 likely) but no other passenger year is confirmed. Do not widen this anchor without a timetable; do not delete it to tidy the map. Frequency: one train each way in the 1890 listing.
